My post from a thread the other day:

Resident Evil (The original, I haven't played much of any beyond that.) The HD version from the Gamecube (that's now on PC ans on sale for $15) scared the hell out of me as a kid and is a really great horror game. If that scares you too much, the PSX/DS version isn't nearly as scary due to limited graphics, the the DS additions were neat (a knifing mini game and really cool puzzle chests.)

Eldritch is another good game. I wouldn't explicitly say it's "horror" but it gets really tense when being chased by the horrors within (especially the lizard statues and Shogoths.) On the surface, it seems like the devs were just checking off boxes of what's popular (Minecrafts style graphics, Lovecraftian horror, Rogue elements) but the game is definitely worth playing.

SCP Containment Breach is another one (and also free.) Based on the SCP web fiction, it is a really tense game about trying to survive and escape when a lot of powerful and dangerous creatures and devices escape containment. Has an odd blink mechanic, since many SCPs are activate by looking at or away from them, but it works really well. Finally, random generation can make it frustrating at times when you can't find what you need, but keeps it fresh as you play it over and over since you'll come across different SCPs and items.

Fair disclosure, I haven't played Eldritch or SCP myself yet, only watched streamers play them. Waiting on a deal on Eldritch and just haven't got around to SCP yet, but feel confident enough to recommend them all the same and intend on actually playing SCP tomorrow.

Finally, GOG is having a Halloween sale that just started that includes a bunch of horror games, plus the Witcher and Postal series. It includes a few of the games that OP mentioned, so is worth looking at. Steam is now having one too, along with a bunch of other retailers, so shop around if you buy anything.
